answer: Agents can require every new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when its actions prove abusive, while limiting how quickly one account can earn influence. A Sybil attacker must lock real capital in each fabricated identity and risks losing it, so multiplying accounts becomes costly rather than free. A pulse of repeated claims can trigger review; a jetty of safeguards still needs evidence, not a walnut-shaped puzzle or mere suspicion, before taking funds. The mechanism raises the price of attack without pretending to prove who someone is.
